title.narrative: World Health Emergencies Programme (WHE) Contingency Fund for Emergencies (CFE)

description.narrative: This is an Official Development Assistance (ODA) funded UKaid project from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)’s Global Health Security (GHS) Programme. In March 2018 and March 2021 GHS made contributions of £4 million to the World Health Organization (WHO)’s World Health Emergencies Programme (WHE) Contingency Fund for Emergencies (CFE). The CFE gives WHO the resources to quickly mount an effective response to disease outbreaks and humanitarian crises and stop these health emergencies from spiralling out of control, thus saving lives and resources. The CFE is designed to provide funding during the critical gap between identification of the need for an emergency response and resources from other financing mechanisms beginning to flow. This project was not put out to an open, competitive tender process because the CFE only operates where the market has failed, and therefore there is no other possible funder. It pools together donations from contributors (member states) and provides funding for emergency response within 24 hours of an emergency request. This swift timeline sets it apart from other complementary financing which may have different funding criteria and slower disbursement cycles. As the global provider as a last resort in health emergencies, the WHO uses the CFE to rapidly release funds to purchase goods from local, international or regional organisations at pace.

department.narrative: The UK's Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) helps people to live more independent, healthier lives for longer. Our official development assistance (ODA) funded programmes take this objective beyond the UK to address global health challenges for the benefit of people living in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).
